cards.text: The wall around Jerusalem is done, friend, and now it's time to dedicate it. So the Levites get sought out from all their homes and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate. ALL their homes. That means even the Levite who never answers the group chat.

cards.question: The Levites have arrived in Jerusalem for the dedication of the wall. What is this celebration going to sound like?

answers.text: Thanksgiving songs with cymbals and harps
A long silent time of prayer
A solemn reading of the Law

cards.text: The singers get gathered up too, from the villages they had built for themselves around Jerusalem. But before anybody celebrates, the priests and Levites purify themselves.

cards.question: After purifying themselves, the priests and Levites purify the people, the gates and the ___.

cards.text: Now Nehemiah, the governor, tells this next part himself (Nehemiah 12:26). He gathers the leaders of Judah and appoints two great thanksgiving choirs.

cards.question: Nehemiah has two great thanksgiving choirs ready to go. Where do they march for the dedication of the wall?

answers.text: Along the top of the wall
Around the outside of the city

cards.question: The first thanksgiving choir sets off along the top of the wall to the right. Which gate is it headed toward?

cards.text: The DUNG Gate, friend, and that choir is singing thanksgiving the whole way there like it's the front door of a palace. Following them are Hoshaiah with half the leaders of Judah, some priests with trumpets, and Zechariah with his associates and their instruments.

cards.question: Zechariah and his associates play the musical instruments prescribed by ___ the man of God.
Nehemiah himself leads the first thanksgiving choir's procession.

cards.text: At the Fountain Gate they go straight up the steps of the City of David, passing above the house of David, all the way to the Water Gate on the east. Singing AND climbing steps, friend, and I get winded walking from the oven to the cooling rack!

cards.question: The second thanksgiving choir heads off to the left along the top of the wall. Who follows it with half the people?

cards.text: That second choir marches right past the Tower of the Ovens, and friend, I've got six stations and thought I was living LARGE, but a whole TOWER of ovens?! They keep going past gate after gate and finally stop at the Gate of the Guard.

cards.question: The two thanksgiving choirs went opposite ways along the wall. In the end, both choirs stand together in the ___ of God.

cards.text: In the house of God, the priests are standing there with their trumpets. Then the choirs sing out with Jezrahiah directing, and I bet that man had both arms going.
That same day they offer great sacrifices, and there's rejoicing. Not polite clapping, friend. REJOICING.

cards.question: Jerusalem is rejoicing at the dedication of the wall. Why are the people so full of joy?

answers.text: God had given them great joy
The king had canceled their taxes

cards.question: Only the men got to join in the rejoicing at the dedication of the wall.
How far does the sound of Jerusalem's joy carry on the day the wall is dedicated?

answers.text: It stopped at the city gates

cards.text: From AFAR, friend, and back in my junk drawer the loudest thing was the dead batteries I shared it with arguing over who had charge left, and nobody heard THAT outside the drawer. That same day, men are put over the storerooms, and the portions the Law sets for the priests and Levites come in from the fields of the villages.

cards.question: The people of Judah bring portions from their fields into the storerooms for the priests and Levites. Why?

answers.text: They rejoiced over the priests and Levites serving
The king of Persia had ordered them to
They were afraid a famine was coming

cards.text: The priests and Levites do the service of their God and the service of purification, with the singers and gatekeepers right alongside them. Everybody's got a station, and trust me, I know a thing or two about stations.

cards.question: The priests and Levites serve the way King David and his son ___ had prescribed.

cards.text: Long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, one of the Levite singers (1 Chronicles 15:16-19), there were directors for the singers and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. And in the days of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who went up to Jerusalem with the priests and Levites (Nehemiah 12:1), and in the days of Nehemiah, the singers and gatekeepers get daily portions.

cards.question: In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, only the richest families gave the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers.
The Levites get daily portions too, and they set aside daily portions for the descendants of ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pull this batch out of the oven for now, friend. Nehemiah's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'The wall around Jerusalem is done...', 'So the Levites get sought out...', 'ALL their homes.' and 'That means even the Levite...'. The limit for an opening card is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The question asks where both thanksgiving choirs march, and the right answer 'Along the top of the wall' covers both of them. The second choir going along the top of the wall is in 12:38, but the card cites only 12:31, which is too narrow.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The card tells about 'Zechariah with his associates and their instruments'. The associates and their instruments come from 12:36, but the card cites Nehemiah 12:31-35, which is too narrow.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: No story card ever tells that Ezra the scribe led the procession (12:36). The baker only answers a true or false card saying Nehemiah did not lead it, so they never learn who did. Ezra is also never introduced, yet card 12 offers 'Ezra the scribe' as an answer.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two beats: the directors for the singers in the days of David and Asaph (with Asaph introduced), Zerubbabel introduced with his background, and the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers. Its second sentence is also very long.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
